text: Not a cloud between here and the lighthouse, and the deck's warm under my feet. Parov Stelar, with Graham Candy. The Sun. [dryly] For once, a song that's telling the truth.
Grey and dripping out there. Parov Stelar and Graham Candy, The Sun, played purely as a request to whoever's in charge upstairs.
Look over at the island right now, all lit up, the lighthouse white as a sugar cube. Weezer, Island in the Sun. I'd go ashore, but then who'd play it.
[quietly] Nobody awake but me, the lighthouse and maybe you. Oasis, Champagne Supernova. Seven and a half minutes, and the dark out there is big enough to hold all of it.
Light's coming up over the water and Opa's had his first coffee, which is to say diesel. Dub Pistols, with Ashley Slater. Back to Daylight. Welcome back.
Fog all round. I can hear the ferry and not see it, and the lighthouse is just a glow. Simon and Garfunkel, The Sound of Silence. It's never been more accurate.
Step out on deck for this one if you can. Clear sky, every star switched on. David Bowie, Starman. If one of them's waiting up there, he's got a good view of the Zeemeeuw.
There's Mars, I think, over the lighthouse. Or a very determined plane. Bowie, Life on Mars?. Either way, I'm asking the same question.
There's a proper swell running, and somewhere a surfer is very happy and I'm holding my mug with both hands. The Beach Boys, Surfin' U.S.A.
The water's catching the light and throwing it straight into the wheelhouse. The Cat Empire, Brighter Than Gold. That's about right.
Shapes in the fog. A buoy, a fishing boat, or nothing. Skip the Use, Ghost. Gerrit's gone very quiet in his crate.
Hot enough on deck that the tar's gone soft. Paul Kalkbrenner, Sky and Sand. The sky's doing its part. Sand you'll have to imagine.
